page.layout: One page of text, two columns of running text in one block; no margin notes. Running head at top centre; page number at foot right area with catchword-like line "Non" at the very foot.

main_text.p: Statue ergo,paterno eum erga te effe animo,& te filium γνώσιον optimo confilio castigari.
6. Immensa eius sapientia est. Ergo cū te explorat & tentat, etsi finem non statim uides,tamen statue id optimum esse, quòd is Deo cognitus & probatus est.
7. Immensa quoq; eius potentia est.Potest igitur suos liberare ab omni malo.
8. Non irascitur in æternum. Psal.103.9. Non in perpetuum rixari solitus, nec in seculum iram custodire.

p.i: Cum autem in temetipsum descendis,hæc consolationum capita, inter multa alia,occurrunt.

main_text.p: 1. Aduersa etiam summa & acerbissima,non efficiunt,ut aliquid nobis decedat. Luc.21.18. Pilus capitis ueftri non peribit. Psal.34.20. Tuetur omnia ossa eius: unum ex ipsis non frangitur.
2. Immò ea plurimum conferunt. Psal. 119.67. Priusquam humiliarer,ego uagabar: sed nunc sermonem tuum custodio.
71. Bonum est mihi quòd afflictus sum, ut discam edicta tua.
3. Deus multò mitius tecū agit,quàm peccatis tuis sis promeritus. Psal.103.10.

page.notes: Text as printed in one block; the line "Cum autem in temetipsum descendis,hæc consolationum capita, inter multa alia,occurrunt." is a centred italic heading-like line set apart, kept as italic paragraph. The Greek word "γνώσιον" in the first line is set in Greek, transcribed as printed in the scan (doubtful: may read γνώστον / γνώσιον). Printed "ftatue" (statue) and "Pfal." references kept. Line "71." and "Priusquam" as printed. Several words in the scan are blurred at the Greek word and at "Psal.103.9" line end; marked uncertain only where the reading is not clear. Printed text: "ftatue" occurs in verse 6 as "statue" (ftatue). Right column of Latin "sed nunc sermonem tuum custodio." ends at the page's second column before the catchword "Non".
